what: Zero-shot transfer diagnostic: does the MAST-U shape->m_s surrogate transfer to Device-C?
interpretation: CORRECTED MECHANISM (per Phase-D review): the design loop steps along the NORMALIZED autodiff gradient of log m_s, ranks candidates by argmax of predicted m_s, and accepts only on TRUE-m_s improvement -- all INVARIANT to a strictly-monotone output transform. So the ~4x under-prediction / range compression are PROVABLY HARMLESS to the loop and CANNOT explain the zero-shot loss. The loss is caused by local gradient-DIRECTION / response-surface distortion of the transferred surrogate on Device-C: zero-shot-vs-retrained gradient cosine = 0.63 (marginal 0.50, mid 0.79), i.e. the transferred gradient points in a substantially different direction than the Device-C-native one, worst in the marginal band. The global Spearman 0.79 is a RANK statistic and does not measure local gradient fidelity. Retraining repairs the local response surface (not the calibration), recovering the MID regime (zero-shot 17% -> retrained 72%) but NOT marginal (27% -> 36%). NOTE the zero-shot framing was the pre-registered 'learned physics, not geometry' test: the learned m_s is NOT a transferable absolute model across devices (it loses 22% to reduce-kappa, p=0.0002) and requires per-device retraining (~704 true 80-mode solves -- the per-device solver budget amortization was meant to avoid), after which it still only TIES. See data/device2_design_deepdive.json.
